stem: The student wants to provide an example of a road diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A road diet is a street redesign that reduces the number of travel lanes.
• The freed space is typically given to bike lanes, sidewalks, or turning lanes.
• Planners often pursue road diets to slow traffic and reduce collisions.
• In 2014, Fremont Avenue in the city of Port Ellery was narrowed from four lanes to two, with the space given to protected bike lanes.
• Collisions on Fremont Avenue fell by 31 percent over the next three years.
choices: Road diets, which reduce a street's travel lanes, are often pursued by planners hoping to slow traffic and reduce collisions.
In the three years after Fremont Avenue was redesigned in 2014, collisions on the Port Ellery street fell by 31 percent.
Port Ellery's Fremont Avenue, narrowed from four lanes to two in 2014 to make room for bike lanes, is one road diet.
Many cities have used road diets like the one on Fremont Avenue to reduce their collisions by roughly 31 percent.
explanation: The goal asks for an example, so you need one named instance tied to the category. Choice C names Fremont Avenue and links it to the category by calling it a road diet. It also shows the defining feature, a cut in travel lanes, even though the note about Fremont Avenue never uses the term 'road diet.'

A.why: You picked a statement about the whole category. It defines road diets and gives their purpose, but it never names a specific street, so it is a generalization, not an example.

B.why: You saw a specific street and stopped there. This choice gives a result on Fremont Avenue but never says the street lost travel lanes or calls it a road diet, so it isn't tied to the category.

D.why: You accepted a claim the notes don't support. The 31 percent drop applies only to Fremont Avenue, and the notes say nothing about 'many cities' getting the same result.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about spillover effects. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• When a minimum wage rises, workers earning slightly above the new minimum often receive raises too.
• Economists call this a spillover effect.
• Employers are thought to grant these raises to preserve pay differences between job levels.
• In 2019, economist Rania Delacroix examined wage records from 1,200 grocery stores after one state's minimum-wage increase.
• Workers earning up to $2 above the new minimum saw average raises of 4 percent.
choices: When minimum wages rise, workers paid just above the new minimum often receive raises as well, as employers preserve pay gaps.
After one state raised its minimum wage, Delacroix found that grocery workers paid up to $2 above it got raises of 4 percent.
Spillover effects ensure that every worker in a state receives a raise of about 4 percent whenever its minimum wage rises.
In 2019, economist Rania Delacroix studied wage records from 1,200 grocery stores following a state minimum-wage increase.
explanation: A generalization makes a claim about the whole phenomenon without making any single case its subject. Choice A describes what usually happens when minimum wages rise and why employers do it, which is a broad claim about spillover effects.

B.why: You picked the wrong level. This is one study's finding about one state's grocery workers, so it's a specific instance of a spillover effect, not a generalization about spillover effects.

C.why: You went for a broad-sounding claim that goes too far. The notes say workers slightly above the minimum 'often' get raises. They never say every worker does, and the 4 percent figure comes from a single study.

D.why: You chose a description of the study's methods. It names a specific study and says nothing about what spillover effects are or what they do.

stem: The student wants to provide an example of a building that uses a passive control device. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tuned mass dampers are heavy weights mounted near the top of tall structures.
• They sway opposite to a building's motion, reducing vibration.
• Because they require no external power, engineers classify them as passive control devices.
• The Kestrel Tower, an office building in Halbrook, has a 410-ton steel pendulum suspended between its 88th and 91st floors.
• This tuned mass damper reduces the tower's sway in high winds by up to 40 percent.
choices: Tuned mass dampers, which require no external power to operate, are classified by engineers as passive control devices.
The Kestrel Tower's 410-ton steel pendulum reduces the office building's sway during high winds by up to 40 percent.
Like other tall buildings, the Kestrel Tower uses a powered steel pendulum that is driven to sway opposite the wind.
The Kestrel Tower relies on a passive control device: a tuned mass damper hung between its 88th and 91st floors.
explanation: An example names one instance and connects it to the property in the goal. Choice D names the Kestrel Tower and says it relies on a passive control device, identified as a tuned mass damper. The notes use 'passive control device' only for the category, so you have to see that the tower's damper belongs to that category.

A.why: You chose the category statement. It explains why tuned mass dampers count as passive devices but never names a building, so it isn't an example.

B.why: You were drawn by the specific building. This choice gives the pendulum's effect but never says it is a tuned mass damper or a passive device, so it doesn't link the instance to the property in the goal.

C.why: You missed a reversal. The notes say these devices need no external power, which is what makes them passive. Calling the pendulum 'powered' and 'driven' contradicts that.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about intaglio techniques. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Intaglio is a family of printmaking techniques in which an image is cut or etched into a metal plate.
• In all intaglio methods, ink is pushed into the plate's recessed lines and the surface is wiped clean before printing.
• Engraving, one intaglio method, uses a sharp tool called a burin to cut lines directly into the plate.
• Etching, another, uses acid to bite lines into a plate coated with a protective ground.
choices: Whereas engraving uses a burin to cut lines directly, etching uses acid to bite lines into a plate coated with a ground.
In intaglio techniques, ink fills lines cut or etched into a metal plate, while the plate's surface is wiped clean.
All intaglio techniques use acid to bite lines into the surface of a metal plate that has been coated with a protective ground.
Engraving, an intaglio technique, relies on a sharp tool called a burin to cut lines directly into the surface of a metal plate.
explanation: A generalization about intaglio techniques has to be true of the whole family, not of one method. Choice B states what all intaglio methods share: ink held in recessed lines on a metal plate whose surface is wiped clean.

A.why: You chose a comparison of two specific methods. Setting engraving against etching describes instances. It doesn't make a claim about intaglio as a category.

C.why: You fell for a choice that sounds general. Using acid on a coated plate is how etching works, and engraving cuts lines with a burin, so the claim isn't true of all intaglio techniques.

D.why: You picked the wrong level. This describes engraving, which is one named method within intaglio, so it works as an example rather than a generalization.

stem: The student wants to provide an example of a vaccine that contains a weakened pathogen. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Live attenuated vaccines contain a pathogen that has been altered so it cannot cause serious disease in healthy people.
• Because they closely mimic natural infection, these vaccines often produce long-lasting immunity.
• Inactivated vaccines instead contain pathogens that have been killed.
• Jonas Salk's polio vaccine, introduced in 1955, is an inactivated vaccine.
• Albert Sabin's oral polio vaccine, introduced in 1961, is a live attenuated vaccine.
choices: Albert Sabin's oral polio vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine, meaning it contains a poliovirus that has been weakened.
Live attenuated vaccines, which contain weakened pathogens, often give long-lasting immunity by mimicking natural infection.
Jonas Salk's polio vaccine, introduced in 1955, is an inactivated vaccine, meaning it contains a poliovirus that was killed.
Sabin's oral polio vaccine, like all vaccines, contains a weakened form of the pathogen against which it offers protection.
explanation: You need one named vaccine linked to the property 'contains a weakened pathogen.' The notes describe that property as 'altered so it cannot cause serious disease' and call these vaccines live attenuated. Choice A names Sabin's vaccine, identifies it as live attenuated, and says outright that its virus is weakened.

B.why: You chose the category-level statement. It describes live attenuated vaccines in general and names no specific vaccine, so it can't serve as an example.

C.why: You found a specific vaccine but from the wrong category. Salk's vaccine contains a killed virus, not a weakened one, so it's an example of something other than what the goal asks for.

D.why: You missed the false generalization inside this choice. The notes say inactivated vaccines contain killed pathogens, so not all vaccines contain weakened ones.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about the effects of community health worker programs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Community health workers (CHWs) are trained members of a community who connect residents with health services.
• Studies across many countries have found that CHW programs tend to increase rates of vaccination and prenatal care.
• In 2018, the district of Moraba launched a CHW program that enrolled 340 workers.
• Within two years, the share of pregnant women in Moraba attending at least four prenatal visits rose from 41 to 63 percent.
choices: Community health workers are trained members of a community who help connect fellow residents with available health services.
Because Moraba's program raised prenatal visits by 22 points, CHW programs everywhere will likely produce similar gains.
Across many countries, programs employing community health workers have tended to raise rates of vaccination and prenatal care.
After Moraba launched its CHW program in 2018, the share of women attending four or more prenatal visits rose to 63 percent.
explanation: The goal asks for two things: a generalization, and one about effects. Choice C makes a broad claim about CHW programs in many countries and states their effect, which is higher rates of vaccination and prenatal care.

A.why: You found a generalization but didn't check its focus. This defines who community health workers are. It doesn't say what CHW programs achieve, and effects are what the goal asks about.

B.why: You accepted a claim that stretches one case too far. A single district's result can't show that programs 'everywhere' will produce similar gains.

D.why: You picked the wrong level. This reports what happened in one district, Moraba, so it's a specific instance of an effect rather than a generalization about CHW programs.

stem: The student wants to provide an example of an ancient refuse deposit that revealed what a community ate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A midden is a deposit of discarded material, such as shells, bones, and broken pottery, left by a past community.
• Archaeologists value middens because household waste can reveal what people ate and made.
• A shell midden 4 meters deep at Cape Voller has been dated to about 3,000 years ago.
• A team led by Ingrid Saltmarsh found mostly fish bones in its lower layers and mostly mussel shells in its upper layers, suggesting a shift in diet.
choices: Middens, which are deposits of discarded material left by past communities, can reveal what people ate and what they made.
Ingrid Saltmarsh led a team of researchers who studied a 4-meter-deep deposit of discarded material at Cape Voller.
At Cape Voller, the midden's lower layers held mostly mussel shells, while its upper layers held mostly fish bones.
The 3,000-year-old midden at Cape Voller, a deposit of discarded shells and bones, revealed a shift from fish to mussels.
explanation: The goal asks for one specific refuse deposit tied to what it showed about diet. Choice D names the Cape Voller midden, describes it as a deposit of discarded shells and bones (the goal calls this 'refuse'), and states the dietary finding: a shift from fish to mussels.

A.why: You chose a statement about middens as a category. It names no specific site, so it can't be an example.

B.why: You were drawn by the named site and researcher. This choice never says what the deposit revealed about diet, and diet is the property the goal asks you to show.

C.why: You didn't check the order of the layers. The notes put fish bones in the lower layers and mussel shells in the upper ones, and this choice reverses them.

stem: The student wants to make a generalization about the temperatures of hot Jupiters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Hot Jupiters are gas giant exoplanets that orbit very close to their stars.
• Many complete an orbit in under 10 days.
• Because of this closeness, their surface temperatures typically exceed 1,000°C.
• Ravel-4b, a hot Jupiter discovered in 2021, orbits its star every 2.7 days.
• Astronomers have measured Ravel-4b's dayside temperature at about 2,100°C.
choices: Ravel-4b, a hot Jupiter that orbits its star every 2.7 days, has a measured dayside temperature of about 2,100°C.
Orbiting very close to their stars, hot Jupiters typically have surface temperatures that exceed 1,000°C.
Hot Jupiters are gas giants that orbit so close to their stars that many complete an orbit in under 10 days.
Like Ravel-4b, all hot Jupiters reach dayside temperatures of about 2,100°C because of their short orbits.
explanation: A generalization about hot Jupiters' temperatures has to make a claim about the whole category and address temperature. Choice B does both: hot Jupiters typically exceed 1,000°C because they orbit so close to their stars.

A.why: You picked the wrong level. This reports one planet's temperature, so it's an example of a hot Jupiter rather than a generalization about the category.

C.why: You found a generalization but missed what the goal names. This is about orbits, and the goal asks specifically about temperatures.

D.why: You accepted a generalization built from a single case. Ravel-4b's 2,100°C is one measurement, and the notes say only that hot Jupiters typically exceed 1,000°C.
